- Today p95 ~860ms (normal ~120ms), p99 ~1.4s

Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident or routing issue? This is impacting several paying customers.

Thanks,

Thanks Naomi and Carlos for the data — I grabbed the sample. Quick summary of what I'm seeing from our side:
- There's a clear RTT uplift for the EU handful of POPs that correlate with traces where connections are being proxied through our us-west routing cluster.
- BGP/peering looks stable; traffic is being handoff-routed per our policy table but the chosen egress path has an unusually high queuing delay (~200-400ms extra).
- No GPU starvation on serving fleet; tokens/sec unchanged.

Initial mitigation: I'm planning a temporary policy override to pin Medlytics traffic to EU egress only, bypassing the problematic US handoff routes. That should drop p95 back near baseline within 5–10m.

I need NetOps to validate the policy change window and confirm rollback plan. Also requesting routing logs for the 21:30–22:30Z window for deeper analysis.

-Vivek
VP, Serving Infrastructure

Attachment: selected_handoff_traces_excerpt.txt (text)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.example, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Cc: eng-oncall@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 08 May 2027 23:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency spike — p95/p99 up for hosted API in EU region

Confirmed with NetOps — an automated traffic shift triggered by a recently deployed egress selector rule sent a subset of EU client flows to a US aggregation cluster (intended for a different CIDR range). The rule had a priority inversion combined with an incomplete CIDR mask in one region.

Action taken:
- Rolled back the policy and applied an emergency override that pins production EU flows to EU egress.
- Monitoring shows p95 falling to ~140ms within the first 6 minutes after the rollback.

Customer communication: Naomi — please send a concise update to Medlytics summarizing what happened, what we changed, and our next steps (postmortem + preventive controls). I can produce a short timeline and the logs for the RCA.

-Jonas
Director, Network Reliability
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2027 00:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95/p99 up for hosted API in EU region

Carlos — quick update from our side.

What happened (brief):
- We identified a misconfigured egress selector that caused a subset of EU-origin traffic to be routed via a US aggregation cluster, adding extra network hops and queuing delay.
- NetOps rolled back the rule and applied a policy override to keep EU flows on EU egress.

Immediate impact:
- p95 reduced from ~860ms to ~140ms within ~6 minutes after mitigation. p99 followed the same trajectory. Error rates returned to baseline.

Next steps:
- Jonas and Vivek will produce an RCA and the router logs for the 21:30–22:30Z window (ETA: EOD Monday 2027-05-10).
- We'll propose a preventive control: automated CIDR-range validation in deploy pipelines and an egress-selector integration test (ETA for rollout: 2 weeks).

We deeply regret the disruption to your users — if you'd like a post-incident call, I'm available this afternoon (13:00–17:00 UTC).

Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
